reviews.title: creates a geometry-backed 30/70 threshold Measurement and preserves it through Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: Creating a 30/70 Measurement from a selected source-time range produces both semantic thresholds and preserves the same Measurement identity and behavior through Save/Open.
reviews.reason: The end-to-end geometry-backed create and actual file round trip are essential acceptance for the Measurement feature and are not implied by schema-only coverage.

reviews.title: updates Annotation style and label offset without waveform regeneration
reviews.primaryContract: Applying style and label-offset changes updates only Annotation presentation while preserving its identity and leaving waveform/local geometry unchanged.
reviews.reason: The zero-regeneration claim is explicitly tied to renderer counters; retain this architecture/performance contract in integration, while a separate concise UI test covers actual style effect.

reviews.title: snaps a dragged endpoint to exact rendered cycle geometry
reviews.primaryContract: Dragging an Annotation endpoint to a rendered semantic cycle boundary commits the exact source boundary and clears temporary snap feedback after pointer release.
reviews.reason: This is the representative pointer-to-shared-geometry interaction; a unit round-trip alone cannot prove the production handle uses the rendered boundary and commits it.

reviews.title: Snap OFF changes annotation endpoint interaction to free geometry
reviews.primaryContract: With Snap disabled, a real endpoint drag uses free geometry and does not expose cycle-snap feedback.
reviews.reason: This is a concise user-visible alternative-mode contract and is distinct from the snapped endpoint journey; keep both focused paths.

reviews.title: Snap toggle and zoom preserve the derived candidate service without mutation
reviews.primaryContract: Changing Snap and Zoom refreshes the derived candidate service while leaving Canonical, History, Dirty state, and waveform projection untouched.
reviews.reason: The assertion is specifically about internal session/candidate and render counters, which is an architecture/invalidation guard; preserve it outside ordinary PR E2E.

reviews.title: preserves canonical source-cycle anchors through an Axis Break snap
reviews.primaryContract: Snapping across a collapsed TimeGroup changes the displayed geometry but retains the correct canonical source-cycle anchor.
reviews.reason: This crosses fold mapping, pointer snapping, and canonical source-time persistence; the focused geometry property suite cannot establish that the Annotation overlay uses the shared Axis Break mapping.

reviews.title: nudges by 1/10 px and cancels pointer preview without a commit
reviews.primaryContract: A sub-threshold Annotation pointer movement canceled before release leaves Canonical, History, and Dirty state unchanged.
reviews.reason: This guards the production pointer lifecycle's no-op/cancel boundary, which is not proven by command-unit tests; it is short enough for focused PR coverage.

reviews.title: moves the whole Annotation by visual offsets and resets offsets independently
reviews.primaryContract: Moving an Annotation visually changes its offset without mutating its semantic anchor, and resetting the offset restores the baseline independently.
reviews.reason: The contract spans a real overlay interaction and distinct canonical anchor-versus-presentation state; keep one focused user journey rather than duplicate this behavior across every Annotation kind.

reviews.title: creates standard and Custom Measurement profiles with explicit transition semantics
reviews.primaryContract: Standard and Custom Measurement profiles select explicit transition semantics and produce the corresponding semantic endpoints.
reviews.reason: This verifies profile authoring and semantic transition selection across the production interaction, not just Measurement schema acceptance; retain it as integration coverage.

reviews.title: edits Measurement semantics with one history step and preserves them through Undo/Redo and Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: Measurement semantic edits commit as one History unit, restore exactly through Undo/Redo, and survive production Save/Open.
reviews.reason: History restoration and file round-trip are separate from profile creation and threshold rendering; preserve this high-risk lifecycle contract in the heavy integration tier.

reviews.title: cancels an active Annotation drag when New replaces the document
reviews.primaryContract: Replacing the document while an Annotation pointer gesture is active cancels the preview and prevents stale drag state from mutating the new document.
reviews.reason: This is a compact cross-document lifecycle boundary with a data-safety consequence; it cannot be replaced by a normal drag or document-epoch unit test alone.

reviews.title: keeps semantic alignment through reorder, zoom, and scroll without waveform regeneration
reviews.primaryContract: The Annotation remains aligned to its semantic source anchor after row reorder, Zoom, and horizontal Scroll, without rebuilding waveform projection.
reviews.reason: The alignment is observable behavior, but its no-regeneration assertion is an internal renderer architecture guard; retain this representative cross-transform check in integration rather than PR.

reviews.title: ripples and clamps Annotation anchors through Timeline edits with Undo and Redo
reviews.primaryContract: Timeline insert/delete operations ripple or clamp Annotation anchors according to the semantic contract and Undo/Redo restores exact prior anchors.
reviews.reason: The interaction crosses two semantic command families and reversible anchor adjustment; this distinct integration contract should not be multiplied into the general Annotation drag matrix.

reviews.title: creates a transition Arrow with two snapped clicks and cancels pending capture with Escape
reviews.primaryContract: Two production pointer picks create a transition-anchored Arrow, while Escape cancels an incomplete capture without leaving a pending interaction.
reviews.reason: This is the representative two-point capture and cancellation user journey; direct handler tests would not verify transition picking or Escape ownership.

reviews.title: creates a Dependency (not just an Arrow) with two snapped clicks when Dependency is the selected Annotation type
reviews.primaryContract: Choosing Dependency before the same two-transition capture creates a Dependency semantic entity rather than silently creating an Arrow.
reviews.reason: This protects the type-selection-to-semantic-entity boundary that the Arrow capture journey does not cover; it is a distinct regression with a short production path.

reviews.title: Annotation Bottom keeps a stable collection while selection, import, and Save/Open remain canonical
reviews.primaryContract: The Annotation collection remains stable while selection is view-only, visibility and import follow their semantic contracts, and imported data survives Save/Open.
reviews.reason: This single broad acceptance journey spans selection, visibility, import, and real file round-trip; do not split it into repeated app-start journeys without evidence that the split improves feedback or diagnosis.

reviews.title: Highlight Position Mode is editable in the Bottom Panel and commits through the existing annotation.setPositionMode command
reviews.primaryContract: The Bottom editor commits the existing Highlight position-mode command once, supports a fractional Free anchor, and rejects an invalid switch back to Cycle Snap without an extra History entry.
reviews.reason: This concise visible path checks the existing semantic command and rejection behavior through the real editor; unit tests complement but cannot prove Bottom editor wiring.

reviews.title: Fractional Highlight Free position survives production Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: A fractional Free Highlight position is serialized and restored unchanged through the production Save/Open path.
reviews.reason: This is the only production serialization round-trip for fractional free-position data and must remain in integration/nightly rather than being inferred from the edit journey.

reviews.title: Annotation Inspector edits the selected endpoint offset through one semantic command
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector applies the selected stable Annotation endpoint's anchor fields as one operation and keeps the committed source identity/coordinates visible.
reviews.reason: The no-waveform/local-geometry-regeneration assertions inspect internal render counters; preserve the useful Inspector journey as an integration architecture guard, not routine PR E2E.

reviews.title: Marker's Vertical span is editable in the Bottom Panel, dispatching the existing annotation.updateVerticalSpan command
reviews.primaryContract: Marker vertical-span fields remain draft-only until Apply, commit in one operation, and the resulting handles move without changing the Marker anchor.
reviews.reason: This is the representative Bottom Draft/Apply plus pointer-handle interaction for a distinct Marker capability; retain it as a focused production journey.

reviews.title: Ribbon Bold applies to every selected Annotation as one atomic commit, each keeping its own color
reviews.primaryContract: A multi-selection formatting action commits once, updates every selected Annotation, and preserves each entity's independent non-font properties.
reviews.reason: This verifies atomic production selection and batch preservation across heterogeneous Annotation types; it is a multi-step journey better retained in integration than routine PR E2E.

reviews.title: renders distinct product presentation for text, callout, marker, ranges, and brackets
reviews.primaryContract: Representative Annotation kinds remain visually distinguishable through their user-facing bodies, borders, and bracket glyphs.
reviews.reason: The six-kind rendered presentation sweep inspects computed DOM styling and distinct shape affordances; retain it in visual acceptance instead of the routine semantic PR profile.

reviews.title: Callout label holds real multi-line text in the live DOM and exported SVG
reviews.primaryContract: Applying a multi-line Callout label preserves its line breaks in the live Annotation and emits each line in the actual SVG export.
reviews.reason: This checks immediate Export of an applied multi-line draft; the separate Save/Open journey proves persistence after document replacement, so the shared output shape is covered at two distinct lifecycle boundaries rather than duplicated in PR.

reviews.title: Bracket's exported SVG carries its own cap marks, not a plain Range line
reviews.primaryContract: The actual SVG export renders Bracket's cap glyphs as a distinct shape rather than falling back to a plain Range line.
reviews.reason: This protects a Bracket-specific exported glyph absent from the other Range/Marker export checks; preserve the production download/export assertion in the heavy tier.

reviews.title: Marker's exported SVG carries a vertical tick glyph, not an invisible zero-length line
reviews.primaryContract: The Marker SVG export contains a visible vertical tick with non-zero height, corresponding to its semantic glyph.
reviews.reason: The Marker-specific vertical tick differs from the Vertical Line export contract and must stay separately asserted at the export boundary.

reviews.title: Callout's multi-line label survives a real Save/Open round trip, in both the live DOM and the exported SVG
reviews.primaryContract: Multi-line Callout text retains line boundaries in the live overlay and SVG export after production Save/Open.
reviews.reason: The real serialization/replacement path is the unique persistence contract not covered by immediate export; keep it in the heavier integration tier.

reviews.title: a test MCP client can connect, read the live document/selection, and request a view-only operation with zero Canonical/History/Dirty delta
reviews.primaryContract: A real external MCP client handshakes, reads live document/selection/viewport context, and requests a visible view-only operation without Canonical, History, or Dirty changes.
reviews.reason: This is the sole end-to-end external process/client path; it spawns the bridge and depends on a fixed port, so keep it out of routine PR parallelism and exercise it as integration.

reviews.title: propose_edit builds a Preview only -- it never auto-validates or auto-applies, and a human must still Validate + Apply it themselves
reviews.primaryContract: An external MCP proposal is only a Preview until a human explicitly validates and applies it; proposal creation alone has zero document/history/dirty delta.
reviews.reason: The external-client trust boundary is distinct from the built-in AI workflow and requires a real bridge process; retain one external path in integration rather than running the child service in every PR job.

reviews.title: an unauthorized propose_edit call (bad token) never reaches the document, and an empty query is rejected before building any proposal
reviews.primaryContract: Bad credentials and empty external proposal requests are rejected before touching the active document or creating a proposal.
reviews.reason: The bridge authorization/input boundary is security-sensitive and requires the actual HTTP endpoint; retain one focused external integration assertion, separate from UI-level AI validation.

reviews.title: rejects a request with an invalid token, and rejects any tool outside the exposed whitelist
reviews.primaryContract: The external bridge rejects unauthorized calls and unexposed tool names and does not report a disabled invalid-token client as connected.
reviews.reason: Whitelist enforcement and page connection-status truthfulness are not fully covered by the malformed-proposal test; this remains a distinct security boundary through the real HTTP server.

reviews.title: bridge disconnect is surfaced truthfully, and the same tab recovers on its own once the bridge comes back
reviews.primaryContract: The connected client status clears after the external bridge exits and the same editor tab reconnects and resumes a real read after the bridge restarts.
reviews.reason: The test controls an external child-process lifecycle and retry loop; keep it in the heavier external integration tier rather than normal PR execution.

reviews.title: AI provider domains use one preview/apply SemanticCommand path
reviews.primaryContract: Representative Group, Signal, Timeline, Bookmark, TimeGroup, Annotation, and Transaction edits all pass through Preview/Validate/Apply with one canonical operation each; view-only fit leaves document/history unchanged.
reviews.reason: The seven-domain scenario is a broad cross-command integration journey, not a single fast AI parser contract. Retain it as broad coverage but exclude it from per-change focused verification.

reviews.title: AI proposal uses preview, deterministic validation, atomic apply, and exact persistence
reviews.primaryContract: An AI semantic proposal remains unapplied until approval, commits atomically as one History entry, supports Undo/Redo, and is preserved by production Save/Open.
reviews.reason: This combines proposal safety, History restoration, and file persistence into the primary product lifecycle; retain it as integration acceptance rather than multiplying the same full journey across more query types.

reviews.title: AI proposal rejects a stale revision after an intervening semantic edit
reviews.primaryContract: A proposal based on an obsolete Canonical revision is invalidated after a separate user edit and never overwrites that edit.
reviews.reason: This is the compact highest-risk stale-proposal guard: one intervening semantic edit proves Preview freshness at the production Validate boundary without the heavier Save/Open workflow.

reviews.title: AI Apply reports a stale proposal through the shared Problems diagnostic path
reviews.primaryContract: Attempting to Apply a stale proposal preserves the intervening edit and reports the shared actionable AI_PREVIEW_STALE diagnostic.
reviews.reason: The first stale test validates before the stale attempt; this one deliberately exercises direct Apply and the shared Problems route, a separate user-visible failure path.

reviews.title: AI preview cannot cross an Open document epoch when IDs and revision are unchanged
reviews.primaryContract: Opening a different document with matching entity IDs and revision still invalidates the old proposal; a fresh proposal then applies to the new document.
reviews.reason: Document-epoch freshness is distinct from revision freshness and requires production Open; preserve it in integration/nightly rather than adding another routine PR file-import journey.

reviews.title: AI Ribbon is a compact Ask/Edit trigger matching other tabs' geometry, with a truthful provider status
reviews.primaryContract: The AI Ribbon trigger fits the Home tab's height, uses a bounded icon, and presents a truthful offline provider status while the assistant opens in Bottom.
reviews.reason: The key assertions compare computed icon and Ribbon geometry plus visible provider status; retain the width-independent desktop visual check in the visual tier, complementing the two responsive clipping cases.

reviews.title: AI Settings default to Always require approval, and every Preview/Validate/Apply is recorded in the Activity Log
reviews.primaryContract: The default requires human approval and Preview, Validate, and Apply each produce ordered Activity Log records with the applied outcome.
reviews.reason: This product governance/audit journey spans three stages and initial Settings defaults; retain as one integration contract rather than multiplying per-event log assertions across workflows.

reviews.title: Auto-apply view-only operations applies a view-only proposal immediately, but never a document-mutating one
reviews.primaryContract: The opt-in shortcut may apply a validated view-only intent, but a document mutation still waits for explicit human Validate and Apply.
reviews.reason: This is a compact safety boundary comparing both proposal kinds under one setting; it cannot be reduced to a unit test because it proves the actual approval controls and History outcome.

reviews.title: Scope switches between Selection / Current View / Document, and Current View genuinely refuses to edit a hidden signal
reviews.primaryContract: Current View refuses to propose edits for a hidden selected entity, while Selection and Document scopes retain their distinct permission behavior.
reviews.reason: The scope contract depends on production visibility, selection, validation, and Apply; retain this multi-policy journey in integration and avoid duplicating the same hidden-entity matrix per operation type.

reviews.title: AI Ribbon tab and Bottom AI Assistant panel stay readable and unclipped at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At 1280x720, the AI trigger, query/scope/Preview controls, Settings, and Activity Log remain horizontally inside the viewport and the primary controls remain vertically accessible.
reviews.reason: The compact viewport exercises width-dependent clipping; retain it alongside the desktop case because the contract explicitly covers responsive AI controls.

reviews.title: AI Ribbon tab and Bottom AI Assistant panel stay readable and unclipped at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: At 1672x941, the AI trigger, query/scope/Preview controls, Settings, and Activity Log remain inside the desktop viewport with the expected panel geometry.
reviews.reason: The desktop geometry is the reference-width counterpart to the 1280x720 clipping case; retain both because they protect different width-dependent constraints.

reviews.title: Combined keeps Transaction and Cycle source boundaries aligned after column resize
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction start, semantic phase boundary, and end remain screen-X aligned with matching Cycle boundaries before and after production column resizing.
reviews.reason: This is a focused visible cross-pane geometry contract using the real layout editor; DOM geometry assertions are necessary to prove the shared-axis invariant and are not replaced by state/unit tests.

reviews.title: Combined left rail hosts the production Transaction Tree beside the Signal pane's frozen columns
reviews.primaryContract: Combined composes the production Transaction Tree and Cycle frozen columns without overlap, and tree selection is view-only.
reviews.reason: The first case verifies actual panel geometry plus stable selection/history behavior. It protects Combined-specific composition rather than duplicating standalone tree tests.

reviews.title: standalone Transaction Mode and Cycle Mode are unaffected by the Combined left panel change
reviews.primaryContract: Combined left-tree sizing does not leak into standalone Transaction mode, and Cycle mode retains its own frozen rows without the Transaction tree.
reviews.reason: The mode-isolation assertions protect distinct runtime composition boundaries and complement, rather than repeat, the Combined layout case.

reviews.title: #573 performance fixture enables horizontal and independent vertical scroll at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: A 10k-cycle, transaction-heavy Combined document supports horizontal overflow, independent pane vertical scrolling, bounded pane mounting, splitter limits, and zero canonical mutation.
reviews.reason: The realistic large fixture and 90-second bound exercise virtualization and scroll/splitter interactions that are inappropriate for every PR run; it is direct #573 closure evidence and must remain scheduled.

reviews.title: #573 performance fixture enables horizontal and independent vertical scroll at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At the compact supported viewport, a 10k-cycle Combined document retains real horizontal/vertical overflow, independent pane scroll, minimum heights, and view-only state.
reviews.reason: The compact viewport has independent clipping and minimum-height risks; the width variant is not redundant with desktop and remains nightly/performance-only.

reviews.title: Cycle Mode default 100% pitch renders at the document's real geometry width, not viewport-fit
reviews.primaryContract: At 100% zoom the presentation scale remains near native geometry scale, and Fit All followed by reset returns to the document geometry width.
reviews.reason: This protects the semantic meaning of 100% zoom and the recovery path after viewport-fit; it is a focused geometry contract, not a screenshot threshold test.

reviews.title: #598 frozen Cycle columns stay fixed and clip time content at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: During horizontal time scrolling, frozen labels keep their screen position and width, clip overflow, remain above scrolling content, and keyboard resizing changes width without Canonical mutation.
reviews.reason: Frozen geometry, clipping, stacking, and keyboard resize are observable layout contracts. The desktop viewport checks the reference-width arrangement.

reviews.title: #598 frozen Cycle columns stay fixed and clip time content at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At compact width, frozen columns stay pinned/clipped while the time pane scrolls, and keyboard resizing remains view-only.
reviews.reason: Compact width changes clipping pressure and available timeline space; this variant independently protects the responsive layout contract.

reviews.title: Cycle ruler labels increment by 1 at 100% zoom on a document with more than 80 cycles
reviews.primaryContract: When adjacent cycle boundaries have sufficient screen pitch, displayed ruler labels remain contiguous by one even on documents longer than 80 cycles.
reviews.reason: This guards presentation tick thinning independently from semantic geometry coverage and avoids a brittle fixed total-tick expectation.

reviews.title: Cycle ruler and grid pitch remain invariant through horizontal scroll at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Horizontal scrolling changes the visible range but not the screen pitch of known source cycles, and Ruler/Grid pitch stay mutually aligned without Canonical, History, or Dirty changes.
reviews.reason: This directly protects the shared time-axis geometry invariant across actual wheel scrolling; the desktop width is the primary routine focused acceptance.

reviews.title: Cycle ruler and grid pitch remain invariant through horizontal scroll at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At compact width, horizontal scrolling preserves known source-cycle pitch and ruler/grid alignment without document/history/dirty changes.
reviews.reason: Compact width alters scroll range and clipping; retain as a visible responsive counterpart while the desktop contract runs in integration.

reviews.title: keeps geometry Grid aligned with the Ruler through view-only zoom
reviews.primaryContract: The same semantic Cycle boundary remains aligned between ruler and geometry grid through a view-only zoom, without canonical revision, history depth, or render-counter changes.
reviews.reason: This is a fast core geometry contract with explicit zero-mutation assertions and belongs in PR-level focused coverage.

reviews.title: renders a clockless axis and preserves it through Save/Open and SVG export
reviews.primaryContract: A clockless document displays a Time axis and preserves that semantic state through Save/Open and SVG export, without fabricating a Clock waveform.
reviews.reason: This crosses axis projection, Save/Open, and export; retain as one end-to-end persistence journey in slower integration/nightly profiles.

reviews.title: hides the reference Clock without losing the axis, then deletes and restores it exactly
reviews.primaryContract: Hiding a reference Clock retains its time-axis identity; deleting it selects defined clockless fallback, and Undo/Redo restores/removes the original stable Clock semantics.
reviews.reason: The visibility/delete/restore lifecycle is a focused stable-ID and fallback contract with exact History assertions, distinct from export persistence.

reviews.title: chooses an explicit reference Clock without fabricating one
reviews.primaryContract: Selecting a real Clock assigns it as reference by stable identity and creates exactly one History unit without fabricating Clock data.
reviews.reason: This is the compact positive selection path complementary to hide/delete fallback and Undo/Redo; it is suitable for focused PR verification.

reviews.title: snaps a clockless transaction against the actual non-first TimeAxis owner row
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction snapping on a clockless axis uses the actual visible TimeAxis owner row rather than a hidden first row, and applies the resulting time to the intended transaction.
reviews.reason: This exercises a real pointer gesture and the shared owner selection in a concrete non-first-row fixture; retain as focused integration coverage.

reviews.title: Transaction clipboard preserves semantic fields and uses fresh IDs
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction duplication preserves semantic metadata and timing while allocating a fresh stable ID; copying itself is view-only.
reviews.reason: This protects semantic copy/duplicate behavior and stable ID allocation through production commands; it is distinct from table deletion targeting.

reviews.title: Bottom Transaction editor deletes its displayed stable target
reviews.primaryContract: Deleting a Transaction from the Bottom editor removes the exact displayed stable ID and creates one History operation.
reviews.reason: The test verifies stable target resolution at the user-facing table boundary and its single-undo contract; keep in focused PR coverage.

reviews.title: standalone Spacer clipboard preserves height and creates a fresh ID
reviews.primaryContract: Duplicating a standalone Spacer preserves its semantic height while allocating a distinct stable row ID.
reviews.reason: Spacer height and identity are a distinct clipboard contract from Transaction duplication and are not covered by transaction-only tests.

reviews.title: surfaces a rejected Clock Generator update in the Problems panel, leaves the prior waveform untouched, and clears it once fixed
reviews.primaryContract: A rejected Clock semantic command reports its diagnostic, preserves canonical/history and the prior waveform, then clears the problem after a valid retry.
reviews.reason: This verifies the full rejected-command to Problems-panel recovery path and the no-partial-waveform-mutation guarantee; neither is proven by schema tests alone.

reviews.title: surfaces an Open failure in the Problems panel
reviews.primaryContract: Malformed JSON opened through the production file input yields a structured syntax diagnostic with source location in Problems.
reviews.reason: This is a compact high-value malformed-file boundary that protects user-facing recovery and is suitable for routine PR coverage.

reviews.title: surfaces a localized WaveDrom render failure with signal context and recovery guidance
reviews.primaryContract: A render failure identifies the affected stable Signal and provides actionable recovery guidance without changing Canonical or History.
reviews.reason: Localization by stable Signal ID and actionable recovery text are distinct from parser/command errors and must be verified through the visible production Problems surface.

reviews.title: surfaces a V1->V2 migration warning after opening a legacy document
reviews.primaryContract: Opening a legacy V1 document surfaces a migration warning, and replacing it with a valid V2 document clears that stale diagnostic.
reviews.reason: This verifies migration diagnostics across two production Open replacements and stale-diagnostic clearing; retain it in integration/nightly rather than PR.

reviews.title: surfaces a rejected command in the Problems panel and clears it on the next successful command
reviews.primaryContract: A rejected semantic command exposes its command ID, target stable ID, field path, and time-unit context; a successful correction clears the error.
reviews.reason: The contract covers diagnostic provenance and recovery across an actual editor command; generic Problems rendering checks do not prove those payload details.

reviews.title: keeps a successful file Save successful when Recent-document storage fails
reviews.primaryContract: A successful authoritative download remains successful if optional Recent-document storage fails, with a warning that accurately distinguishes the two outcomes.
reviews.reason: The fault-injected browser storage failure verifies separation of durable file Save from optional metadata persistence and prevents misleading failure reporting.

reviews.title: reports Recent-document storage read failures without crashing
reviews.primaryContract: A Recent-document storage read failure is reported with operation, source, stage, cause, and recovery while keeping the Editor mounted.
reviews.reason: The read path is a separate failure boundary from Save/write failure and uniquely asserts no application crash plus technical diagnostic detail.

reviews.title: keeps a dirty document dirty when the authoritative file Save fails
reviews.primaryContract: If authoritative file Save preparation fails, the Editor reports SAVE_FAILED and preserves the document's Modified state and History.
reviews.reason: This fault injection protects the authoritative-save boundary and dirty/history preservation; it is distinct from optional Recent-storage failure.

reviews.title: surfaces browser download preparation failures for Export
reviews.primaryContract: Failed browser download preparation for export is reported with operation and recovery guidance, while Canonical, History, and Dirty remain unchanged.
reviews.reason: The failure happens at the browser download boundary after SVG generation and must not be conflated with clipboard-write failure; keep as focused integration coverage.

reviews.title: surfaces clipboard write failures for Export
reviews.primaryContract: Clipboard write rejection is surfaced with clipboard-specific operation and recovery guidance without mutating document/history state.
reviews.reason: Clipboard permission failure is a separate external side effect from file download failure, with its own actionable diagnostic contract.

reviews.title: beforeunload guard follows the History dirty state without mutating it
reviews.primaryContract: The beforeunload guard reflects clean/dirty History state through a real edit/Undo lifecycle and itself does not change Canonical or History.
reviews.reason: This is a compact state-safety contract for unsaved navigation protection that cannot be fully inferred from the dirty indicator alone.

reviews.title: Follow Selection OFF freezes the Bottom target; Pin locks in whatever is currently shown, independent of live selection
reviews.primaryContract: Follow Selection OFF freezes the current Bottom target, Pin freezes that displayed target independently of selection, and re-enabling Follow Selection resumes tracking.
reviews.reason: This is the end-to-end proof of the explicit #426 Follow/Pin product contract across three changing selected entities; a settings toggle unit test cannot prove target ownership.

reviews.title: Bottom Pin preserves a selected Group JSON context without view mutation
reviews.primaryContract: Pin preserves the selected Group as the JSON panel context while another Group becomes selected, and Pin/unpin do not change Canonical, History, or Dirty state.
reviews.reason: Group-scoped Advanced JSON context is a distinct consumer of Bottom target ownership, with explicit view-only invariants; it complements the Signal target journey.

reviews.title: Advanced JSON applies a selected object through one document command
reviews.primaryContract: Applying an edited selected Signal JSON object updates its canonical projection through one document command and one History unit.
reviews.reason: The production JSON editor, validation/apply route, canonical row projection, and exact History unit are a user-facing command boundary distinct from typed Inspector edits.

reviews.title: Whole Document JSON stays read-only until Advanced mode and validates before Apply
reviews.primaryContract: Whole-document JSON is read-only in default mode; Advanced mode requires explicit validation before document Apply.
reviews.reason: This small guard protects the destructive whole-document boundary and explicit validation step, which selected-object Apply does not cover.

reviews.title: Advanced JSON applies a selected Group through one document command
reviews.primaryContract: Applying selected Group JSON creates one document command, then Save/Open preserves the Group name and resets History for the opened document.
reviews.reason: This combines entity-scoped Apply with an actual downloaded-file Save/Open round trip. It is intentionally slower and serves persistence integration rather than PR duplication.

reviews.title: Inspector and Bottom expose the documented edit contract surfaces
reviews.primaryContract: Cycle and Transaction modes expose the documented Inspector/Bottom edit surfaces and the shared Follow Selection/Pin controls.
reviews.reason: This checks the mode-dependent edit ownership/availability contract, not the visual layout or behavior of each individual editor control.

reviews.title: Inspector Cancel restores signal and clock drafts without a canonical mutation
reviews.primaryContract: Cancel discards in-progress Signal-name and Clock-generator drafts and leaves Canonical, History, and Dirty unchanged.
reviews.reason: Signal and Clock use different typed draft controls and cancellation affordances; the journey proves both are discarded without command side effects.

reviews.title: Bottom editors cancel transient drafts and preserve canonical counters
reviews.primaryContract: Changing selected Signal discards its uncommitted Inspector draft, preserves document counters, and Transaction Bottom remains a table-first list without a duplicate persistent editor.
reviews.reason: This protects draft retargeting and verifies the removed duplicate Transaction editor has not returned; those ownership boundaries are distinct from explicit Cancel.

reviews.title: Transaction Bottom table keeps selection while Inspector owns edits
reviews.primaryContract: Selecting a Bottom Transaction row selects the same stable target for the Inspector while the Bottom remains a table; the duplicated bottom property Apply surface is absent.
reviews.reason: This is a fast ownership assertion guarding against reintroducing a second transaction-property draft surface and verifies row-to-Inspector target synchronization.

reviews.title: Signal and Group rename use the same explicit Enter/Escape draft contract
reviews.primaryContract: Signal and Group rename commit once on Enter, reject blank names without mutation, cancel transient text on Escape, and Undo restores the prior semantic name.
reviews.reason: The journey compares entity kinds through real Inspector/tree interactions and verifies validation, commit, cancellation, and Undo behavior in the shared draft lifecycle.

reviews.title: Clock Generator toolbar icons render as small inline glyphs, not oversized placeholders
reviews.primaryContract: Clock Generator toolbar icon glyphs remain compact and do not expand to the browser's default oversized SVG dimensions.
reviews.reason: This is a narrow visible affordance regression that is not a semantic command concern; retain in the visual profile instead of routine PR integration.

reviews.title: Bottom Clock validates suppressed slots relative to delayed start
reviews.primaryContract: Clock suppressed-period slots are interpreted relative to a delayed generator start and a valid edit commits as one History operation.
reviews.reason: The delayed-start origin is the semantic edge case and this compact UI command journey gives it a routine regression guard.

reviews.title: Bottom Clock edits update real waveform geometry and edge-counter overlays
reviews.primaryContract: Invalid generator/suppressed-period drafts are rejected without History corruption; a corrected generator updates the waveform, edge-counter settings update overlays, and final valid Apply succeeds.
reviews.reason: This covers end-to-end validation and recovery across waveform and edge-counter surfaces. Exact render-counter deltas are implementation-coupled and should be owned by the existing incremental-invalidation contract suite, not treated as an additional GUI-level acceptance oracle.

reviews.title: Clock Preview renders the draft Period on the selected Clock's real waveform with zero Canonical delta, and reverts on Cancel
reviews.primaryContract: Preview reflects the selected Clock's uncommitted Period draft, preserves Canonical/History/Dirty, and Cancel restores the committed waveform.
reviews.reason: This is the primary preview effect + explicit cancel safety boundary; the preview must be visibly tied to the real waveform rather than a status flag alone.

reviews.title: Clock Preview reverts when the toggle is switched off without Cancel
reviews.primaryContract: Turning Preview off discards the transient waveform and restores the canonical Clock view without requiring Apply or Cancel.
reviews.reason: Toggle-off is an independent exit path from Preview and is not guaranteed by the explicit Cancel test.

reviews.title: keeps all controls reachable in a compact desktop grid
reviews.primaryContract: At the desktop editor width, all Clock Edge Counter controls remain visible and reachable without horizontal overflow or excessive vertical expansion.
reviews.reason: This directly protects the editor's compact control layout and is a visual affordance check rather than a command correctness test.

reviews.title: reflows without clipping at a narrow bottom-editor width
reviews.primaryContract: At 1000px viewport width, the Clock Edge Counter editor has nonzero usable width, no horizontal overflow, and keeps Apply reachable.
reviews.reason: The constrained bottom-editor width is a distinct responsive clipping boundary; retain this narrow-width visual case without running it in routine PR profile.

reviews.title: uses the selected Bookmark identity for marker count-from
reviews.primaryContract: Marker-based Edge Counter uses the selected Bookmark's stable identity and source time through Undo/Redo and Save/Open, producing no labels before that marker.
reviews.reason: This validates stable Bookmark reference identity and persisted Edge Counter semantics across multiple state transitions and file roundtrip; it is intentionally outside PR latency budget.

reviews.title: starts selected-edge counting from the clicked rendered Clock edge
reviews.primaryContract: Selecting a source cycle and using selected-edge counting starts numbering from the preceding real rendered Clock edge, not from a cycle-only fallback.
reviews.reason: This is a real pointer-to-ruler and Edge Counter geometry ownership journey; a pure edge-index test cannot establish that the UI-selected cycle resolves to the rendered source edge.

reviews.title: reuses the production edge index for a 100k-cycle Clock refresh
reviews.primaryContract: On a 100k-cycle Clock, changing Edge Counter presentation reuses the production edge index and performs zero per-cycle probes or geometry lookups.
reviews.reason: This asserts implementation counters on an explicitly large fixture; keep it in performance/nightly where cost matters and do not treat internal counter names as user-facing browser assertions.

reviews.title: keeps an empty group consistent across Left Tree, Bottom Group dropdown, Undo/Redo, and Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: An empty Group remains represented consistently in the virtualized Left Tree and Signal editor dropdown, retains stable identity through rename/delete/Undo/Redo, and roundtrips with zero rows through Save/Open.
reviews.reason: This exercises multiple projections, virtualized visibility, semantic lifecycle, and actual file roundtrip; it is a high-value but slow cross-surface acceptance rather than routine PR coverage.

reviews.title: creates three distinct empty groups without omissions or duplicates
reviews.primaryContract: Creating multiple empty Groups allocates distinct stable IDs and exposes exactly the same set in the Left Tree and Group selector.
reviews.reason: This compactly protects duplicate/omitted entity projection under repeated creation and compares two production surfaces by ID rather than display order.

reviews.title: renders the first signal inserted into an initially empty group
reviews.primaryContract: Inserting the first Signal into an initially empty Group mounts one row with the same new stable ID in Left Tree, frozen labels, timing rows, and waveform ownership.
reviews.reason: This is a concise first-child projection regression. The target is resolved as the stable-ID set difference, avoiding DOM order/last-node identity assumptions.

reviews.title: Insert Ribbon and Left Tree Add menu never offer Pulse; Event is still a real creatable Signal type
reviews.primaryContract: New authoring paths offer Event but not legacy Pulse, and Event creation/edit/Undo/Redo remain functional from Ribbon and Left Tree Add surfaces.
reviews.reason: This guards the explicit product distinction between current Event creation and legacy Pulse compatibility across two production creation surfaces.

reviews.title: loads, edits, persists and exports a legacy Pulse Signal without breaking it
reviews.primaryContract: An existing legacy Pulse loads as Pulse, remains editable through the value editor, survives Undo/Redo and Save/Open, and is preserved in JSON plus SVG/PNG/PDF exports.
reviews.reason: This is explicit backward-compatibility protection across file and three export formats; its size and lifecycle breadth justify slower integration/nightly execution.

reviews.title: Delete uses one selection command across Ribbon, context menu, and keyboard
reviews.primaryContract: Ribbon, context-menu, and keyboard Delete remove the selected stable Signal through equivalent behavior, each restoring it with one Undo.
reviews.reason: This directly guards command-adapter parity at three production interaction surfaces and one-step Undo; the compact single-signal path is suitable for routine PR verification.

reviews.title: Document Properties legend reorder actions are named and keyboard operable
reviews.primaryContract: Legend reorder actions expose accessible names, communicate disabled boundaries, and support keyboard activation while changing the visible stable-ID order.
reviews.reason: The previous test froze private icon SVG/path counts; it now proves the actual accessible action and keyboard-reorder behavior independent of the icon implementation.

reviews.title: Export respects a collapsed TimeGroup: shorter SVG width, no hidden cycle numbers, source data unchanged
reviews.primaryContract: SVG export applies the same collapsed TimeGroup projection as the editor, omits hidden cycle labels and Axis Break markers, and does not alter source document data.
reviews.reason: This proves user-visible export projection parity for shared time mapping; on-screen fold behavior alone does not establish the downloaded SVG's geometry or labels.

reviews.title: browser SVG export keeps adversarial document text inert
reviews.primaryContract: Adversarial document text is XML-escaped as text and cannot create active script, event-handler, image, or javascript URL content in exported SVG.
reviews.reason: This is a concise security boundary at the actual user-triggered SVG export path; lower-level escaping tests cannot prove the composed export artifact is inert.

reviews.title: keeps File ribbon controls named and removes no-op blank slots
reviews.primaryContract: File Ribbon exposes only named, visible, focusable, non-overlapping actions, and key File dialogs can be opened at the supported desktop widths.
reviews.reason: This is a responsive layout/affordance audit at multiple widths rather than a command semantic test; keep in the visual profile to protect no-op/blank slot regressions.

reviews.title: Comment Row Line Spacing follows the same Draft -> Apply contract as Title/Body (no per-keystroke History entries)
reviews.primaryContract: Changing Comment Row line spacing stays local until Apply, commits the completed draft once, and Cancel restores the last committed value without changing History.
reviews.reason: This compact visible Draft/Apply/Cancel journey protects the historical per-keystroke Semantic Command regression and the user-observable History boundary; state-only tests cannot prove the wired control path.

reviews.title: Font Family/Size/Color commit once on blur or Enter, and Clear formatting is scoped and no-op when already clear
reviews.primaryContract: Font Family, Size, and Color each commit one History unit at their documented completion boundary; repeated blur and Clear Formatting when already clear do not create extra History entries.
reviews.reason: This single journey crosses three distinct editor completion events plus scoped clear/no-op behavior. Keep the complete semantic lifecycle in integration rather than adding its multi-commit sequence to every PR run.

reviews.title: non-Home design-system primitives own stable button and icon geometry
reviews.primaryContract: The non-Home design-system ribbon button primitive preserves its documented minimum hit width, button height, icon dimensions, label containment, and token value.
reviews.reason: This deliberately isolates the reusable design-system primitive and its token geometry, so keep it out of semantic PR journeys and in the visual contract profile. It is a primitive-level check, not evidence that every production Ribbon surface mounts the primitive.

reviews.title: non-Home dialog close buttons are named, non-submit actions that restore their invokers
reviews.primaryContract: Hierarchy, Bulk Registration, and Save As close actions are accessible named buttons, do not submit forms, close the active dialog, and return focus to the invoking control.
reviews.reason: The assertion is now about accessible control behavior and focus restoration rather than SVG viewBox/path implementation details; three distinct dialog owners stay covered by one concise production journey.

reviews.title: app-owned dialogs close with Escape without changing the document
reviews.primaryContract: Escape closes each top-level app-owned dialog, focus remains trapped while open and returns to its invoker, and closing the dialog leaves Canonical revision and History unchanged.
reviews.reason: This intentionally traverses five independent dialogs and verifies focus cycling, Escape cancellation, focus return, and document non-mutation; it is valuable integration coverage but too broad for the routine PR path.

reviews.title: Home overflow uses the shared menu keyboard behavior and restores its invoker
reviews.primaryContract: The Home overflow menu opens with focus on its first enabled action, supports Home/End navigation, and Escape closes it and restores focus to the trigger.
reviews.reason: This is a compact user-visible keyboard and focus contract for the common overflow menu, independent of the SVG or DOM implementation used by its actions.

reviews.title: floating Find and Time Scale dialogs trap focus and restore their triggers
reviews.primaryContract: Find/Replace and Transaction Time Scale dialogs keep keyboard focus within the open dialog and return focus to their respective triggers after Escape.
reviews.reason: The test protects two distinct floating-dialog owners, including the Cycle-to-Transaction mode transition, so it remains integration coverage rather than duplicating the short PR dialog journey.

reviews.title: Tree menus close on Escape or outside click without selecting the canvas
reviews.primaryContract: Tree Add/More menus dismiss on Escape or a real outside pointer click, restore focus to the menu trigger, and leave document, selection, and dirty state unchanged.
reviews.reason: The outside path now uses a real browser click rather than manually dispatched pointer/click events and checks that selection is preserved; this is a concise production interaction boundary.

reviews.title: Ctrl+D duplicates the selected Signal as one canonical command with a fresh stable ID
reviews.primaryContract: Ctrl+D duplicates the selected Signal through the command route and produces exactly one new unique stable Signal identity without depending on rendered row count.
reviews.reason: This is a single keyboard-to-semantic-command path with stable-ID uniqueness assertions; its identity contract is not established by testing the command handler alone.

reviews.title: Ctrl+A selects every Signal without mutating the document
reviews.primaryContract: Ctrl+A selects the current Signals without changing canonical revision or History.
reviews.reason: The browser-level shortcut routing boundary and view-only state guarantee are concise and distinct from text-input native select-all behavior.

reviews.title: Ctrl+A inside a text input performs native select-all instead of the app shortcut
reviews.primaryContract: Ctrl+A in an available Signal name input performs native text selection and does not select the Signal collection; the test requires the editor input instead of silently skipping the contract.
reviews.reason: A native editable control is the exception boundary for the global shortcut. Requiring the field prevents a missing Inspector control from making the test pass without checking the behavior.

reviews.title: Escape cancels an in-progress Annotation drag, closes the context menu, and resets dependency-arrow pick
reviews.primaryContract: Escape cancels a live Annotation drag without Canonical/History changes and clears dependent transient interaction state so later menu or Dependency gestures cannot inherit stale interaction state.
reviews.reason: This combines pointer cancellation with context-menu and two-click Dependency state cleanup, so it is a multi-owner interaction lifecycle better suited to integration than routine PR coverage.

reviews.title: shared ValueSignal policy keeps Quick Values renderable through Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: Quick Value authoring creates an Event value accepted by shared ValueSignal policy, remains renderable, and survives the actual Save/Open round trip.
reviews.reason: The actual file round trip and renderer readiness validate backward-compatible persisted value semantics beyond the isolated schema/conversion tests; retain outside routine PR verification.

reviews.title: incompatible State to Binary conversion is rejected before canonical commit
reviews.primaryContract: An incompatible State-to-Binary conversion is rejected with visible feedback and leaves canonical revision, History, and Dirty state unchanged.
reviews.reason: This proves the Inspector's production conversion route rejects a value-domain violation without mutation; pure validator tests cannot verify rejected UI Apply wiring and user feedback.

reviews.title: Pulse is never offered as a Type conversion target, even from a value-domain-compatible Level (logic) signal
reviews.primaryContract: The removed Pulse type is absent as a conversion target in both Inspector and Bottom Signal editors, while the current Level source remains selected.
reviews.reason: The test guards the user-facing policy in two independently wired type selectors and is distinct from loading/editing legacy Pulse documents.

reviews.title: compatible Bus to State conversion supports Cancel, Apply, Undo/Redo, and Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: A compatible Bus-to-State conversion is discarded on Cancel, committed once on Apply, restored through Undo/Redo, and persists through actual Save/Open.
reviews.reason: This is a distinct persistence/History compatibility journey crossing draft, apply, Undo, Redo, and file replacement; it is intentionally excluded from the fast PR profile.

reviews.title: Bus to Binary conversion rejects non-logic values without mutation
reviews.primaryContract: A Bus containing non-logic tokens cannot convert to Binary; the visible rejection leaves canonical revision, History, and Dirty state unchanged.
reviews.reason: This shares the conversion-rejection owner with State-to-Binary but covers a separate data/value-domain failure case and its explicit error; keep both compact cases in the same PR contract family.

reviews.title: Event Table exposes one action route and visibly rejects invalid imports
reviews.primaryContract: The Event table presents one route for each row/import/export action, rejects malformed import through its production file-input route, and preserves canonical revision, History, and Dirty state.
reviews.reason: This combines a compact action-surface duplicate guard with the security/state boundary for invalid user-provided import data; no lower-level parser test proves the file-input interaction.

reviews.title: Event Table valid import uses canonical validation and one history entry
reviews.primaryContract: A valid Event import passes canonical validation, updates the Event rows, and creates exactly one History entry.
reviews.reason: Valid import is the positive counterpart to rejection and proves the actual file control reaches one semantic commit instead of merely checking parser output.

reviews.title: switches Ribbon tab content without touching Canonical, History, WaveDrom, RowLayout, geometry, or Inspector/Bottom state
reviews.primaryContract: Switching Ribbon tabs preserves workspace position and does not change document or Inspector/Bottom visibility state.
reviews.reason: Cross-tab state preservation is product behavior, but internal renderer counters and CSS group-class assertions make this too broad for routine PR; replace implementation-specific checks with observable state assertions.

reviews.title: Insert tab creates a real canonical Signal through a SemanticCommand
reviews.primaryContract: The Insert Ribbon action creates a Signal through the production command path and records one history mutation.
reviews.reason: This verifies a Ribbon entry point reaches a canonical command and History, not only that the button is rendered.

reviews.title: Review tab Problems button navigates to the Problems panel
reviews.primaryContract: Activating Problems from the Review Ribbon exposes the Problems panel without document mutation.
reviews.reason: A distinct navigation affordance with one direct user-visible assertion and low runtime.

reviews.title: AI query previews and applies one scoped SemanticCommand
reviews.primaryContract: The Ribbon AI route previews without mutation, validates locally, and applies one scoped rename as exactly one History unit.
reviews.reason: The shared AI contract exists elsewhere, but this exercises the Ribbon-to-Bottom-panel entry route; retain only if this entry distinction remains intentional.

reviews.title: AI preview cancellation leaves Canonical and History unchanged
reviews.primaryContract: Canceling an AI preview preserves the canonical revision and History and leaves the selected target available.
reviews.reason: Isolates the unique cancellation boundary; stale-revision behavior is covered by the fuller AI proposal workflow contract.

reviews.title: View exposes stable Show/Panels/Guides/Zoom/Workspace/Layout slots
reviews.primaryContract: View commands are discoverable and usable while display-only toggles leave Canonical and History unchanged.
reviews.reason: Combines group topology, primitive internals and display behavior; keep in visual profile and separate implementation-coupled structure checks from product behavior.

reviews.title: View zoom uses a shared view-only route and does not move Home presentation
reviews.primaryContract: View zoom updates shared zoom, keeps Home controls coherent, and does not change document revision or History.
reviews.reason: Bounding-box and slot assertions are layout-coupled; this belongs outside routine PR verification.

reviews.title: View groups compress without horizontal overflow at 1280px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1280px the View Ribbon remains usable without horizontal overflow and key controls remain visible.
reviews.reason: This viewport-specific overflow contract belongs in the visual gate, not every PR run.

reviews.title: View group controls stay inside their owned regions
reviews.primaryContract: Rendered controls remain within their visual group bounds and adjacent fit controls do not overlap.
reviews.reason: Reads internal DOM children and CSS rectangles directly; preserve the invariant but prefer a component/layout contract or a concise visual assertion independent of the current group primitive.

reviews.title: Layout Focus Waveform restores the previous panel state without document history
reviews.primaryContract: Focus Waveform hides Inspector and Bottom, then restores the previous preset and Bottom visibility without document mutation.
reviews.reason: A short production UI-state round trip with visible outcomes and a view-only invariant.

reviews.title: View Panels toggle buttons show a selected border/color accent, not a persistent blue-tile fill (#389)
reviews.primaryContract: Checked pane toggles communicate selection without a persistent hover-like fill and differ visually from unchecked controls.
reviews.reason: Computed color/border checks encode a visual design contract and belong in the visual profile.

reviews.title: Layout Reset restores application panes without mutating the document
reviews.primaryContract: Reset Layout restores default pane dimensions and edit preset without changing Canonical or History.
reviews.reason: Protects the user-triggered reset contract and its non-document mutation boundary with one concise interaction.

reviews.title: keeps Insert and Timeline groups usable at 1280px
reviews.primaryContract: Insert and Timeline command controls remain visible and non-overlapping at the compact supported viewport while representative commands still work.
reviews.reason: This is a broad, geometry-heavy 1280px case combining two tabs and canonical mutations; keep viewport-specific behavior in visual tier and consider separating its command journeys from layout checks.

reviews.title: keeps Insert and Timeline groups usable at 1672px
reviews.primaryContract: At the canonical wide viewport, Insert and Timeline controls remain discoverable, contained, and usable without overlap.
reviews.reason: The wide viewport is an explicit visual baseline but repeats much of the compact case's journey; retain only the unique wide-layout evidence and avoid making both cases routine PR checks.

reviews.title: Tree Add and Insert Ribbon share the selected row and group insertion target
reviews.primaryContract: Tree Add and Ribbon Insert use the same selected row/group target, preserve insertion position, and Undo restores the prior tree contents.
reviews.reason: This multi-operation journey compares two production entry points and validates placement/Undo parity; its breadth and visual-reference fixture make integration tier more appropriate than PR.

reviews.title: Timeline exposes shared N-cycle and Time Group presentation commands
reviews.primaryContract: Timeline exposes cycle insertion and Time Group collapse/expand controls, and the group view state changes without leaving the editor active.
reviews.reason: Exercises actual Time Group creation and shared outline controls rather than only checking command labels; retain as a representative integration journey.

reviews.title: Time Group outline rows expose mapped spans and shared collapse controls above the ruler
reviews.primaryContract: A created Time Group appears in the ruler outline and its collapse state is reflected by the shared Timeline and ruler controls.
reviews.reason: Adds the distinct ruler-projection surface to the Time Group interaction; keep one representative cross-surface geometry check and avoid duplicating every toggle state at browser level.

reviews.title: Time Group outline exposes Ungroup through the semantic timeline command
reviews.primaryContract: Ungroup invoked from the Time Group outline removes the group through the semantic command path and creates history.
reviews.reason: Protects an independently exposed outline action and confirms group removal, but overlaps the broader create/collapse workflow; retain only while that distinct entry path is required.

reviews.title: Timeline workflow groups keep explicit cycle semantics and aligned controls
reviews.primaryContract: Timeline labels make cycle semantics explicit, controls fit within their groups, and group baselines stay aligned.
reviews.reason: Mixes accessible product labels with direct layout measurements; retain under visual acceptance and move any pure wording checks to a cheaper contract layer.

reviews.title: Timeline group boundaries show a non-overlapping separator with aligned captions at 1280px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1280px Timeline group boundaries remain visible, non-overlapping, and caption baselines align.
reviews.reason: Viewport-specific computed-style/geometry audit belongs in visual tier; compare against the paired viewport case to avoid redundant repeated layout assertions.

reviews.title: Timeline group boundaries show a non-overlapping separator with aligned captions at 1672px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1672px Timeline group boundaries preserve spacing, non-overlap, and a shared caption baseline.
reviews.reason: This is the wide reference measurement paired with the compact case and should not execute in routine PR verification; retain only the unique width-dependent evidence.

reviews.title: Left Tree +Add and Ribbon Insert both select the row they just created (#262)
reviews.primaryContract: Rows created from Tree Add or Ribbon Insert become the active selection, including Signal, Group, Comment, and Spacer insertion routes.
reviews.reason: Covers several distinct row-kind insertion semantics and selection feedback; keep in integration pending consolidation with the adjacent Tree/Ribbon insertion target journey.
